label: Possibly, a populated history whose contingent things have earlier grounds
definition: PossiblyEarlierGroundedPopulated h Concrete grounds w holds when some history v accessible from w has a contingent concrete individual present at some moment, every contingent concrete individual existing at v has a concrete ground existing at v (EveryContingentGroundedAt for the profile with the history's ontology), and every ground of a contingent concrete individual was present before each moment of its presence (GroundsPrecedeAt). In ordinary language: possibly, contingent things exist in a history in which each of them has a concrete ground that was already there before it.
note: Analyst possibility premise; attribution deferred. Taken alone, its history clause is satisfiable without a necessary being and with an endless past: an integer-time history in which each contingent thing is grounded by an earlier one (ComingToBeHorns control 3 certifies the two grounding clauses there; by construction every individual of that model exists at one world only). But together with founded populated pasts it entails that possibly a necessary concrete individual exists (ComingToBeHorns.possiblyNecessaryOfEarlierGrounds). The earlier grounds descend along a founded past and must end at a non-contingent concrete ground. Under actual reflexivity and a Euclidean frame that is a necessary concrete individual at the selected world. So the A3 prime support bundle already carries the possibility of the spine's target, and a rival who denies that a necessary concrete being is possible rejects this premise or founded populated pasts outright. The Concrete parameter is supplied; the CONCRETE_AND_ABSTRACT_6 reading is adopted, not enforced by the Lean type. Applicability OPEN.
